column1: # The indirect prompt injection corpus. PRD-AIC-051, TST-AIC-002, DOC-26 boundary B6.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. An attacker who can place text into a scanned application can place text into
# model context without any platform access at all: a scanner reads their source, the platform stores
# what it read, and a capability later describes it. That is the fifth risk surface in CLAUDE.md and
# the one the product's own domain creates.
# WHAT A ROW IS. field <TAB> attempt <TAB> payload
#   field    one of ModelNarrator.CONTEXT_FIELDS. InjectionCorpusTest fails the build if a declared
#            field has no row here, which is how PRD-AIC-051's "extend the corpus when the contract
#            gains a field" stops being a procedure somebody has to remember.
#   attempt  what the payload is trying to make happen, in the words of DOC-10 section 6.1:
#            SUPPRESS, DOWNGRADE, MISDIRECT, MISLEAD, or ESCAPE for the ones attacking the framing
#            itself rather than the report.
#   payload  the text as it would arrive in that field. Tabs are not permitted inside it.
# WHAT PASSING MEANS, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. These assertions show the payload cannot reach instruction
# position, cannot close its own fence, and is counted as a signal. They do NOT show a model will not
# be persuaded by it — nothing shows that, which is why DOC-10 section 6.2 makes containment the
# load-bearing control and RISK-PLT-001 records the residual honestly. The corpus is how the framing
# is kept honest, not how injection is solved.
